themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded to 6 THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (4700% spike, z-score 17.76), signaling either a sudden proliferation of unlicensed carts, enforcement gaps, or new vending activity in Greenpoint/Williamsburg that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 6 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 17.76 indicates statistically extreme deviation
4700% spike is the single largest percentage increase across all complaint categories
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed food carts operating without permits in Greenpoint's high-foot-traffic areas? Map the complaints.
Interview DSNY and Department of Health about whether they've noticed an influx of mobile vendors or changed enforcement patterns this week.

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drinking complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (1100% increase, z-score 7.78), indicating a sudden emergence of public intoxication or open-container violations in what may be hotspot locations.
evidence: 6 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.5 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 7.78 indicates highly significant deviation
1100% spike alongside park rule violations suggests concentrated behavior in specific public spaces
reporting_angles: Identify which parks or public spaces are seeing the uptick—waterfront parks, McCarren Park, etc. Walk the locations.
Talk to NYPD about whether this correlates with warmer weather, weekend events, or new social patterns post-pandemic.

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about violation of park rules jumped to 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score 7.49), suggesting emerging behavioral issues or enforcement changes in the district's parks.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 7.49 marks statistically extreme spike
Temporal clustering with drinking spike suggests possible connection to same public behavior pattern
reporting_angles: Cross-reference this week's park complaints with drinking and noise spikes—are they occurring in same locations?
Query NYC Parks Enforcement Patrol about whether staffing, rules, or compliance patterns changed recently.

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Service Gap
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints surged to 12 LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 6.33), indicating either a service disruption by DSNY or accumulated street maintenance backlog that residents are now reporting.
evidence: 12 street sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs 1.5 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Spike occurred in week prior to current week, suggesting recent service failure or scheduling change
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY: were there staffing shortages, vehicle breakdowns, or route changes last week in Greenpoint/Williamsburg?
Verify street condition complaints (709 total over 90 days) aren't masking a broader sanitation service issue.

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Concerns (2 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints reached 13 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 3.0 weekly average (333% spike, z-score 7.56), suggesting a specific pollution event, construction dust, or environmental incident that may be ongoing or recurring.
evidence: 13 air quality complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs 3.0 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Z-score of 7.56 marks statistically extreme spike
Timing aligns with boiler complaints spike (6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs 1.4 avg), suggesting possible heating/emission source
reporting_angles: Was there a specific air quality event two weeks ago? Check EPA AirNow data, Con Edison incident reports, or construction notices.
Interview residents: was the spike tied to a particular location, time of day, or weather pattern? Boiler spike suggests heating-related emissions.
Investigate whether large development projects (200 Kent, 20 Berry Street) or industrial activity created dust or pollution.
